subject: Customer-managed keys & operator access for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — scope and transfer plan
messages:

Subject: Re: Private deployment — keystore ownership and operator access questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the call this morning. As we prepare a statement of work and push toward procurement, Legal has asked for a short write-up on three items we need clarified in the DPA/addendum:

1) Custody model for customer-managed keys (we want explicit language confirming customer retains sole control of the CMK and Redwood does not have access unless under an agreed escrow process).
2) Operator access during software updates and incident response (we need to understand what telemetry or transient access Redwood engineers will require for troubleshooting on-prem nodes).
3) Cross-border transfer commitments — we must ensure logs and telemetry do not leave the EU without explicit consent.

We attached the initial list of redlines from Legal (MediCorp_DPA_comments_v1.pdf). Could you and your team propose contractual language and an operational checklist we can include in the SOW? Also, we would like a short diagram showing the keystore handshake and any escrow triggers.

Best,
Eva

Subject: Re: Private deployment — keystore ownership and operator access questions

Eva — thanks for the clear list and the PDF. We read the redlines and sketched a two-part approach: contractual assurances + operational runbook. High level proposal below; I will circulate a tracked DPA addendum and a diagram by EOD tomorrow.

Summary proposal (preview):
- Custody: Redwood will accept customer-managed keys (CMKs). Customer retains exclusive control of the CMK. Redwood will not persist plaintext keys or possess material ability to decrypt customer data.
- Escrow/Breakglass: We propose an escrow process that requires a documented breakglass request, two-person authorization from customer security, and a time-limited, audited access window implemented via ephemeral operator tokens. All use is logged and exported to customer-controlled storage.
- Operator access: For troubleshooting we will use a) telemetry-only diagnostic streams (configurable), and b) ephemeral support sessions triggered by customer tickets. No inbound SSH by default; any elevated access requires pre-specified service accounts and ticket references.
- Data residency: Telemetry and logs can be configured to route to a customer-controlled collector in the EU. Redwood will not replicate telemetry out of-region unless explicitly approved in writing.

Attachments we'll send: high-level keystore-handshake-diagram.png, an escrow-schedule-proposal.xlsx with timing/approvers, and a DPA addendum with tracked language.

Questions for Legal & Security to confirm with you:
1) Is MediCorp comfortable with the escrow model that includes ephemeral operator tokens tied to a signed request?
2) Do you need independent escrow (third-party custodian) or is Redwood-held escrow with customer audit acceptable?

I'll loop in Connor (solution engineering) to confirm implementation details and timeline.

Naomi

Quick technical note and constraints for the runbook:

1) Ephemeral operator tokens: we can issue time-bounded tokens tied to a single ticket id using our identity service. Tokens can be configured for 15/30/60 minute windows. All operator sessions require the token plus an action-specific justification string.

2) Telemetry routing: for VPC/on-prem we provide a collection agent that can be configured to forward to customer-owned ELK/OTLP endpoints; default is not to forward to Redwood's hosted telemetry. Customers must opt-in to any diagnostic upload.

3) Escrow model options:
  - Redwood-managed escrow: Redwood encrypts a copy of an encrypted keystore blob under an escrow key retained in Redwood HSM; release requires signed customer authorization plus multi-person Redwood approval. Pros: faster recovery; Cons: customer may prefer independent third-party custody.
  - Third-party escrow: we can support integration with custodians (e.g., KeyCustodyCo); release still requires customer-specified approval chain.

4) For EU-only residency guarantees: we can block outbound telemetry by default and provide a signed configuration manifest that the customer can use as evidence in procurement. However, logs produced by ephemeral operator sessions (audit trails) will be exportable upon explicit customer direction.

I attached a starter diagram and a proposed escrow schedule (escrow-schedule-proposal.xlsx). If Legal wants specific SLA language on escrow release windows (e.g., release within 48 hours of authorized request), call that out and we'll confirm feasibility.

Karthik

Hi all,

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the attachments — the diagram and schedule look helpful. A few notes from Legal and Security:

- MediCorp is open to Redwood-managed escrow only if we have (1) a third-party notarization step on release and (2) clear audit export to our EU collector. Can Redwood add a notarization workflow (simple PKI timestamping or third-party sign-off) to the release process?
- For operator sessions: security wants the default to be telemetry-only; any elevated support session must require customer ticket ID, two customer approvers, and an independent notarization record.
- For the DPA addendum: please include an explicit clause that telemetry and ephemeral session logs will be stored for a minimum of 90 days in customer-controlled storage unless otherwise requested.

Next steps: please send a tracked DPA addendum with the escrow/notarization language and the runbook with the exact ticket/approval fields. After that we'll schedule a technical review (30 min) to confirm the agent config and to walk our infra team through the collector setup.

Proposed meeting window: Mon 28 Jun 09:00–11:00 CET or Tue 29 Jun 14:00–16:00 CET.
